newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel follows low sulphur down.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel follows low sulphur down.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil fell sharply on Thursday in the wake of low sulphur prices and amid talk of fresh transatlantic barrels heading into Europe, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded early in the morning at $111 fob ARA before weaker crude and poor bunker demand dragged numbers lower. Barges traded as low as $103 fob ARA, and ended at around $105/$106.
High sulphur cargo swaps numbers fell by around $5 a tonne, after physical business was done on Wednesday at $110 cif NWE.

Dealers said some of the weakness was because of talk that at least three cargoes of high sulphur fuel - on the 85,000 tonne Omikronventure L, the 84,000 tonne Progress and the 52,000 tonne Alkman, were likely to arrive in Europe in early February.
These cargoes follow similar deals in December, and the latest barrels are expected to move either to ARA or Romania.

Low sulphur fuel oil recovered some of the day's losses by the afternoon amid a perception that recent hefty falls may have been overdone and after Wednesday's strong surge in crude late in the day. A little trader buying interest has emerged for low sulphur fuel oil, with one dealer saying he might pay around the quoted fob mean.
But end-user demand remains resolutely lacklustre. Low sulphur swaps ended the day at around $109/$110 fob NWE.
